$comment: L2 gloss layer for the ingested Nebraska clause. Batch-drafted, then frozen; reviewed_by records the initial editorial pass — a named human reviewer should confirm it against the clause text before classroom use. Note the clause does three things, not one: it makes the Legislature single-chambered AND reserves initiative and referendum to the people. The gloss covers all three because they are all in the section; it does not reach into neighboring sections.

glosses.grade_5: Nebraska's lawmakers are one group, not two. Nebraska is the only state that does it this way. The people kept two powers too. They can make a law by voting. They can also undo one.
glosses.grade_8: Nebraska puts its lawmaking power in a Legislature of one chamber. It is the only state that does. The same section keeps two powers for the people. Initiative lets them propose a law and pass it at the polls. Referendum lets them approve or reject a law the Legislature passed.
